items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Types have clear names (HeaderHashPolicy, CookieAttribute, SourceIPHashPolicy) and doc comments on every field. Plugin code lives in its own consistent_hash.go with intent-revealing helpers like applyConsistentHash, following the style of the other feature files.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Follows the plugin pattern: types, codegen deepcopy/CRD, a separate consistent_hash.go (~330 lines), a hook into the plugin's Equals/Validate/apply, and merge registration. Unit tests plus a golden translator test. No visible dead code or debug leftovers.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: MinLength=1 markers on the key fields, a CEL rule for disable, and TTL parsing with tests. But Substitution is optional, and it isn't clear from the diff that the regex pattern is validated in the plugin. There's also no HTTPRoute-only target restriction, which the reference has.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: The golden merge output puts the rule policy's entries ahead of the route-wide ones within each type, in the order headers→cookies→queryParameters→filterState. Metadata 'consistentHash' lists both policies under merge.TrafficPolicy.gateway.kgateway.dev. Hidden merge tests pass.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: The empty-policy route produces a single `connectionProperties: sourceIp: true` entry, and the /disabled route has no hashPolicy. A struct-level XValidation rule says 'when disable is true, no other fields may be set', and it appears in the generated CRD.
